### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object inlineActionApiParamsToBodyExtra; a field of const object pageHeaderSubtitleAlias), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object inlineActionApiParamsToBodyExtra; a field of const object pageHeaderSubtitleAlias))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via PageHeaderProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c0f4e7ae77051838da398ed7dcfda69acf71f7f0` — the merge of head `6f0fcb21f4efcdfcd6213ab9ad1675341204ffa8` into base `a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c0f4e7ae77051838da398ed7dcfda69acf71f7f0 && git checkout c0f4e7ae77051838da398ed7dcfda69acf71f7f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb 6f0fcb21f4efcdfcd6213ab9ad1675341204ffa8 && git checkout -B drift-repro a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb && git merge --no-ff 6f0fcb21f4efcdfcd6213ab9ad1675341204ffa8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a1285f26db92269642ebb90ab70fe3840dda51cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f0fcb21f4efcdfcd6213ab9ad1675341204ffa8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23421 (body + 3 comments: triage `6163717752`, claim `6165302231`, dev report `6168805850`), PR #23485 (body, 10-file list, net diff vs `main` at the head; merge base `3d231ba78`), and the 37 check-runs on the head. The premise was verified against the repo tree read-only (`docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/{types,apply,stored,registry}.ts`, `packages/spec/package.json`, `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/spec/src/shared/{strict-object.ts,retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts}`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `AGENTS.md` item 3). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The claim's premised ruling — premise verified, and RIGHT.** The claim (`6165302231`) ruled: retire both conversions from the load path at 18 if ADR-0087 ends the window that way, otherwise stop. The premise holds, read independently of the dev's own premise check: ADR-0087 D2 "Window" (lines 143–144) says each conversion is applied by the loader for one major, "then retired from the load path in N+1"; the section "The load-window's second half is now mechanical" (lines 453–456) names `MetadataConversion.retiredFromLoadPath` as that retirement; `conversions/types.ts` `RetiredConversionState` is `retiredFromLoadPath: true` plus a required `retiredAfter`; `apply.ts:156` skips such an entry unless `includeRetired`; `stored.ts:107` pins `includeRetired: true`. Both entries read `toMajor: 17`, so 18 is N+1. `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` is the right stamp: the package label is `18.0.0-next.0` (prerelease, so the newest published stable is the highest stamp, `17.7.0`, which is also the newest `## 17.x` in `CHANGELOG.md`), and 7 existing entries already carry `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`. The route taken (retire, not "save door applies live-window conversions") is the one the premise licenses. Right.
2. **Accept-set narrowing on the authoring funnel — RIGHT and correctly characterised.** `defineStack` / `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` (`normalizeStackInput`) stop rewriting `page:header` `properties.description` → `subtitle` and an inline `type:'api'` action's object `params` → `bodyExtra`; the author now meets the props-gate refusal. This is the finding's class (b) fix: the save door's raw judgment and the CLI's normalized judgment now agree (the lint pin flip in `validate-component-props.test.ts` asserts both tiers refuse at the same path naming `subtitle`). Right.
3. **Data at rest unchanged — RIGHT.** `applyConversionsToStoredItem` replays with `includeRetired: true`; the artifact-ingestion door decides per entry by `retiredAfter`; `os migrate meta` replays by id. The conversions.test.ts cases now run under `includeRetired: true` for the rewrite properties and add two authoring-posture cases asserting no rewrite and the entry fields. The new case for the button also asserts `ElementButtonPropsSchema` refuses the object form naming `bodyExtra`. Right.
4. **Public-surface text changes (`component.zod.ts`, `action.zod.ts`) — RIGHT, and owed by a gate.** `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` requires every entry whose `retiredAfter` equals the newest published stable release to have a JOIN row, and every prescription it renders to name the derived major (`@objectstack/spec 18` / `protocol 18` via `majorsNamed`) and, for any `os migrate meta --from N`, N = `toMajor − 1` = 16. Neither refusal named a release on `main`, so stamping `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` turns that pin red on exactly these two ids; the producer of the refusal text is the only place that satisfies it. `PageHeaderProps` moves `description` from `aliases` to `guidance` (both are `strictObject` options, `strict-object.ts:158`): the new text names `@objectstack/spec 18`, `subtitle`, and `--from 16`; the pin's `refusal()` reads the parse issue messages and will see exactly that. The `action.zod.ts` object-form `params` refusal keeps its `bodyExtra` instruction and adds "until @objectstack/spec 18" and the `--from 16` sentence; the JOIN row filters issues at path `action`. The only majors named in either text are 18 (the regex does not match `ADR-0087` or `#NNNN`). These two edits are inside the claim's package but outside its file surface — judged under ③. Right.
5. **Vehicle swap to `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen` — RIGHT in substance.** The entry is live (`toMajor: 15`, no `retiredFromLoadPath`, `registry.ts:572`), rewrites the component-level key via `renameVisibilityAlias` emitting `path: ${path}.visibleWhen`, `from: 'visibility'`, `to: 'visibleWhen'`, so `HEADER_PATH = pages[0].regions[0].components[0].visibleWhen` and `retiresIn: 16` (= `toMajor + 1`) are the correct notice. The strict-parse expectation `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` matches `PageComponentSchema.visibleWhen: EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` lowering. The three suites' own docblocks prescribed the re-point. Every assertion is unchanged in substance. One wrong sentence in the diff, flagged under ③ (item c).
6. **Changeset content — RIGHT.** `minor` with the **BREAKING** banner, FROM → TO mapping and one-line fix for both renames, the `os migrate meta --from 16` sentence, the stored-data posture, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker: `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered page-header-subtitle-alias, inline-action-api-params-to-body-extra)`. `already-registered` is an accepted category of `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` for ids that resolve at HEAD and pre-exist the diff; both do (the diff adds two fields to existing entries, no new entry). `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.
7. **`Clause-②` spellings.** The claim declared `Clause-②: no`; the changeset declares `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. What the diff IS: an accept-set narrowing of the authoring funnel with no new accepted shape or export, so the exact spelling is `no (narrowing)` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: "`no (narrowing)` is a truthful `no` to the widening question and a breaking change at the same time"). Both `no` and `yes (narrowing)` are well-formed to `readClause2Line` (the token is first after the colon; the arm is the first word of the parenthetical) and `yes (narrowing)` reaches the same level verdict as `no (narrowing)` (`clean`, at least `minor`, breaking carried by the banner during the launch window, `major` forbidden). The claim's bare `no` is the understatement: it named no arm although its own `Container & model:` line says "(a narrowing)". Acceptable to the gate either way; the `yes` is over-declared, not wrong at the gate. One placement defect in the PR body, flagged under ③ (item b).
8. **In-scope census left for the seat — RIGHT to leave.** The claim asked the dev to list the other `toMajor: 17` entries still live with a verdict each; the report's first `out_of_scope_findings` entry does so (7 flow-node entries overdue, `sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit` overdue but needs an `enumWithRetiredValues` prescription first, `datasource-driver-mongo-to-mongodb` and `retry-policy-converged` deliberately kept and needing a ruling), plus the older-window stragglers including the new vehicle itself. Not this card's diff; the seat files one closing card as the dispatch asked.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`, with the **BREAKING (authoring)** banner and migration, matches what the diff publishes: a narrowing of the authoring accept set in a released package, shipped during the v18 launch window where `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` forbids `major` and requires the banner + ADR-0087 disposition as the breaking-ness carriers (AGENTS.md item 3: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING", "`yes` takes at least `minor`"). `skip-changeset` would be wrong (the package publishes). `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/cli` have test-only edits and correctly carry no changeset. `Check Changeset`: `success`.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — as the changeset declares; the diff's exact arm is `narrowing`, and `no (narrowing)` would be the tighter value. Both spellings are accepted by the gate and grade identically.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report `6168805850`, `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`); `open_questions: []`.

a. **File-surface extension (`ui/component.zod.ts`, `ui/action.zod.ts`, `shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`)** — the claim said "stop on a breach and explain it"; the dev did not stop but explained in the PR body and the report. Answered: ACCEPTED. The extension is forced by a gate the claim itself named ("any D2 bookkeeping the step-18 retirement owes … as the gates name it"): the removal-version pin requires the refusal text to name the release, and the refusal text is produced only in those two schema files. The edits change refusal wording only; no accepted shape moves. The two refusal strings are judged RIGHT in ① item 4.

b. **PR body carries no readable `Clause-②:` declaration** — the PR body mentions `` `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` `` only inside a bullet sentence ("with the **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the FROM to TO mapping…"). `readClause2Line` reads declarations by position (line-initial, with at most a bullet, blockquote marker or bold as decoration); this is the "inline-key" placement near-miss, so `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` read `value: null` from the PR and graded the level axis `not-measured-moot` (exit 0, because spec is already `minor`). The changeset's own line is well-formed and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm there. ESCALATED to the adopting seat as a PR-body edit (no code change): add a bare line `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (or `no (narrowing)`) to the PR body so the level axis is measured, not moot. Not a defect of the head.

c. **One wrong sentence in a docblock** — `packages/cli/src/commands/validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts` lines 63–65 now read "that conversion, `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen`, retired from the load path at protocol 18 and the fixture was re-pointed here". The retired conversion is `page-header-subtitle-alias`; the new vehicle is the live one. Comment-only, no assertion rides on it, but it states the opposite of the truth in the file that teaches the next re-pointer. ESCALATED as a one-line follow-up fix (this PR or the seat's closing card).

d. **The new vehicle is itself overdue** — `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen` is `toMajor: 15` and still live at 18, which the dev's own census names. The three re-pointed suites will need re-pointing again when the family closing card retires it. Answered: noted; the suites' docblocks already prescribe it, and this card's scope is the two entries the finding named.

e. **PR #23418's changeset paragraph and `authoring-rules.ts` comment become false on landing** — both files are in #23418's diff, so this PR correctly leaves them; the dev flagged it as "noted, not filed". Answered: ESCALATED to the seat, who owns both PRs: the later lander (per triage, this card lands with or before #23418) updates the paragraph and the `validateComponentProps` comment, or #23418 takes it into its landing.

f. **Kebab `page-header` source nodes carrying `description` are neither converted nor judged after retirement** — the dev grounds harmlessness in objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` no longer registering `page-header`. Answered: accepted as stated; the same posture already holds for `page:header` `icon` and `breadcrumb`, and the walk still lists the kebab type for data-at-rest replays.

g. **Check-runs on the head** — 22 completed `success`, 6 completed `skipped` (opt-in/matrix placeholders), and 15 **in progress** at brief time: `Build Core`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Test Core (1/6)` … `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`. Read once; no watcher. The queue reads their conclusions when they land; this record does not pre-empt them. Of the completed ones, the gate families this diff touches — `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, the four claim/branch guards — all concluded `success`.

h. **Claim's `Clause-②: no` versus the changeset's `yes (narrowing)`** — judged in ① item 7: no gate couples the two, both parse, the level verdict is the same. No action.
